correctness.rationale: For integer d≥3 the polytope equals [-1,1]^d∩2B_1^d by integral hypersimplex vertices and contains exactly 2d(d−1) exposed roots. All active sign and coordinate facets give the exact illumination criterion (1). Illuminated pairs cannot be disjoint; their graph is a star or triangle. Summing the strict pair inequalities gives a coordinate magnitude greater than the number of illuminated edges in a star, or gauge >3 for a triangle. Hence every source illuminating k vertices costs strictly more than k. Covering all vertices yields the lower bound, and sources (1+epsilon)v approaching each vertex give the matching infimum for the whole boundary. All quantifiers and equality limits hold for d≥3. The included exact rational check independently verifies 137200 finite source patterns in d=3..6, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Kiss–de Wet 2012 singled out quantitative illumination of the cuboctahedron as a natural case but supplied only an upper estimate 12 and conjectured optimality. The exact lower bound answers that gap and, without arbitrary slicing, unifies the cuboctahedron and 24-cell into a canonical root-polytope family in all dimensions. A dimension-free incidence/covering efficiency theorem explains the exact invariant and is useful for further quantitative illumination studies. The contribution is structural rather than a routine tabulated recomputation.
